correctness.rationale: Universal upper construction of weight 2k works at any deleted-matching pair. If weight<2k with n>=2k, each shore has an empty vertex and hence requires at least k incidences on opposite shore, contradiction. At equality either both shores have empties, forcing one occurrence of each color per shore, with matching-index supports by the missing-matched-edge obstruction, or an entire shore is occupied, forcing n=2k, singleton assignments and twice each color. Surjection and multinomial counts are bijections; both directions proved. The direct C++17 incidence checker exhaustively enumerates all functions of weight<=2k for (k,n)=(3,6),(3,7) among others and agrees at exact counts 1446 and 2023; it is not used in lieu of infinite proof. No unproved implications or asymptotic convergence assumptions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general bound gives only upper 2k here; its lower bound min(2n,k) cannot force 2k for k>=3. value.rationale: A full all-optimizer classification for a natural well-studied infinite graph family and all color counts k>=3 is more than an elementary bound or tiny gain. The deleted perfect matching forces the nonobvious coincidence of occupied supports, which yields a Stirling-number sum for every minimum configuration. Exactly at n=2k, a second entirely different family appears and vanishes above that sharp threshold. The result counts optimal dominating sets of the natural prism Cr_n square K_k and supplies exact benchmark multiplicities, e.g. M_{6,3}=1446 and M_{7,3}=2023. The already known k=2 result is not repackaged as new. The parameter and precise count are inherently meaningful and the proof covers infinitely many nontrivial instances.
